cues.en: They're going to write a recursive function for calculating the Fibonacci series in three steps.
So Fibonacci numbers is a different mathematical problem in case if you don't know what it is, let's
just clarify it.
So Fibonacci sequence is a sequence of numbers in which each number is the sum of the two preceding
ones, and the sequence starts from zero and one, and Fibonacci of zero is going to be the zero, and
Fibonacci of one is going to be one.
Now the sequence looks like this.
So it starts from zero and one.
So zero plus one is going to be one.
Then one plus one is going to be two.
And then one plus two is going to be three.
And two plus three is going to be five.
And it continues like this.
So this is how the Fibonacci numbers looks like.
Now we need to create a recursive function to calculate these sequences.
So we are going to pass as a parameter.
For example zero.
It's going to return zero.
If we pass one it's going to return one.
If you pass for example two it's going to return this number which is going to be the index of two.
So it starts from zero one and two.
So if you pass three it's going to return this number, which is two, and it continues like this.
Now the first step to write the recursive function we know that we need to find the recursive case.
So we need to examine this Fibonacci series carefully.
So if we look at over here we can see that first two numbers are zero and one.
Now zero plus one is going to give us the third number which is one.
Then we can continue to the next number.
So one plus one is going to give us the next number which is going to be two.
Then one plus two is going to give us the next number which is going to be the three.
Then two plus three is going to be five and the sequence is going to be like this.
Now this means that for five we can write that five is equal to three plus two.
So it is equal to sum of the previous two numbers.
So we can write the function like this.
Fibonacci n is equal to Fibonacci n minus one plus Fibonacci n minus two.
So this is going to be our recursive case.
So we can put it like this.
And we can write our function like this.
So for Fibonacci and we are going to return Fibonacci n minus one plus Fibonacci n minus two.
So as you can see, for each cases, it's calling the Fibonacci function with the smaller value.
So we have said that in case of recursive function the function calls itself with the smaller value.
So here again you see that in this case the function calls itself two times with small values.
So this is going to be our recursive case.
Now if you just go ahead and create this function it's going to cause the infinite loop.
So this means that we need to create over here base case to stop infinite loop which calls the stack
overflow.
Now we have mentioned before that to be able to identify the base case, first we need to check the
definition of any given problem.
So in this case if you look at this definition we can see that for Fibonacci zero we are returning zero.
And for Fibonacci one we are returning one.
So this means that we can use this part of the definition as a base case.
So we can say that if n is equal to zero or n is equal to one inch this case, we are just going to
return n.
So if we pass it zero over here, it's going to return zero.
If you pass over here one it's going to return one.
So this is going to be the base case for our Fibonacci number.
So with this we have completed the second step also.
Then we can continue to the third step.
Now in the third step we need to identify the unintentional cases.
So in this case we said that Fibonacci sequence starts from zero and one.
So this means that this is not applicable for negative numbers.
So if we call it for Fibonacci minus one or Fibonacci minus two in this case also it's going to cause
the infinite loop.
So to avoid this we are going to write another if condition which is going to cover the unintentional
case.
So if n is less than zero in this case we are just going to return minus one.
So we can go ahead and implement this in practice.
So here before we have created a recursive function.

Then the recursive case was like this.
We are just returning Fibonacci with n minus one plus Fibonacci n minus two.
Then we have said that if you run this function, it's going to cause the stack overflow.
So that's why we need if condition over here.
So if n is equal to zero or n is equal to one.
In this case we are just going to return n.
Now here as a third step, we need to take into account the unintentional case which is going to be
